record.paper_title:
AIM Workshop “Pólya-Schur-Lax Problems: Hyperbolicity and Stability
Preservers” — A List of Open Problems
record.context_brief: Zeros of truncated Fourier transforms of Jacobi theta kernels
record.original_question: For the finite Fourier transform H_R(x)=∫_0^R Φ(t)cos(xt)dt built from the Jacobi theta kernel Φ, are the zeros of H_R in the strip |Im z|<1 for sufficiently large R, and for which R>0.11 does H_R acquire nonreal zeros?

evidence.quote: Problem 33 (D. A. Cardon [20], H. Ki, Y.-O. Kim [52]; see also [32, 35, 36, 37]). Consider the finite Fourier transform Z R HR (x) := Φ(t) cos(xt) dt, 0 where the Jacobi theta function, Φ(t), is defined by Φ(t) := ∞ X   2π 2 n4 e9t − 3πn2

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let
\[
\Phi(t) \;=\; \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \bigl(2\pi^{2} n^{4} e^{9t} - 3\pi n^{2} e^{5t}\bigr)\, \exp\!\bigl(-\pi n^{2} e^{4t}\bigr), \qquad t\in\mathbb{R},
\]
be the Jacobi theta kernel arising in the integral representation of the Riemann xi function (so that $\Phi$ is even, positive, and rapidly decaying as $|t|\to\infty$). For each $R>0$ define the truncated cosine (finite Fourier) transform
\[
H_{R}(x) \;=\; \int_{0}^{R} \Phi(t)\,\cos(xt)\,dt, \qquad x\in\mathbb{C}.
\]
Each $H_{R}$ is an even entire function of exponential type at most $R$.

(a) Prove or disprove: there exists $R_{0}>0$ such that for every $R\ge R_{0}$, all zeros of the entire function $H_{R}(z)$ lie in the horizontal strip $\{z\in\mathbb{C} : |\operatorname{Im} z|<1\}$.

(b) Determine, as explicitly as possible, the set of $R>0.11$ for which $H_{R}$ has at least one nonreal zero, and in particular identify the threshold values of $R$ at which nonreal zeros first appear (or disappear).
artifact.category_tag: Zeros of Fourier transforms and the Riemann xi-function
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem in the AIM workshop problem list on Pólya–Schur–Lax problems. Related work by Cardon, Ki, Kim, and Csordas on Fourier transforms of admissible kernels and the Jacobi theta function establishes partial results (e.g., reality of zeros under various truncations and connections to the de Bruijn–Newman constant), but no source verifies a complete resolution of the strip-localization and nonreal-zero-threshold questions for $H_R$.

status_evidence.title: Fourier Transforms of Positive Definite Kernels and the Riemann ξ-Function
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates the distribution of zeros of entire functions represented as Fourier transforms of admissible kernels, with the Jacobi theta function playing a prominent role.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature provides partial results on zeros of Fourier transforms of the Jacobi theta kernel but does not resolve the strip and threshold questions for the truncated transform H_R.

status_evidence.title: AIM Workshop: Pólya-Schur-Lax Problems — Open Problems List
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 33 concerns the finite Fourier transform H_R of the Jacobi theta kernel and asks about the location of its zeros.
status_evidence.claim: The problem appears on a curated list of open problems.
